lessons.title: Refraction of Light at an Interface

cards.title: 1.1 Refraction of Light at an Interface
body: The bending or change in the direction of propagation of light as it passes from one medium to another is known as refraction.
The ray of light which travels into the second medium is called the refracted ray.

cards.title: Refraction: fuller notes
body: Light changes speed when it passes from one medium to another, so it bends (**refraction**). Going into a denser medium (air → glass) it slows and bends **towards** the normal; goi
**Refractive index** n = sin i ÷ sin r = speed of light in vacuum ÷ speed in the medium (c ÷ v). **Snell’s law:** n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

cards.title: Worked example: refractive index and critical angle
cards.problem: Light travels at 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s in air. Glass has n = 1.5. Find the speed in glass and the critical angle.

cards.title: Refraction & lenses
body: n=c/v. Snell: n₁sinθ₁=n₂sinθ₂. Convex converges; concave diverges.
Lens formula: 1/f=1/v+1/u (sign convention matters — use your textbook’s).

body: When light goes denser→rarer, beyond critical angle you get total internal reflection.

cards.title: 1.3 Optical Instruments
body: A basic compound microscope consists of two converging lenses.
The lens closest to the object is called the objective lens and the other lens closest to the eye is called eyepiece lens.
